title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
summary: ActObs replaces the standard SFT convention of computing loss only on agent action tokens by also supervising the environment observation tokens already present in each trajectory, before running GRPO. It adds no data, parameters, sequence tokens, or forward passes; the cost is a modified loss mask in SFT and the measured pass@1 reliability regression at 8B. It can fail when the deployment budget allows only a single sample (pass@1), since the benefit concentrates in pass@k and exploration diversity, and results are demonstrated only on Qwen3 4B/8B with GRPO on terminal and code-editing tasks.
rationale: The change is a low-cost SFT loss-mask modification compatible with a single 24 GB GPU, but the reported gains depend on sampling budget, model size, and GRPO post-training, so it merits a workload-specific A/B test rather than unconditional adoption.

claims.statement: ActObs replaces the standard SFT convention of computing loss only on agent action tokens by also supervising the environment observation tokens already present in each trajectory, before running GRPO. It adds no data, parameters, sequence tokens, or forward passes; the cost is a modified loss mask in SFT and the measured pass@1 reliability regression at 8B. It can fail when the deployment budget allows only a single sample (pass@1), since the benefit concentrates in pass@k and exploration diversity, and results are demonstrated only on Qwen3 4B/8B with GRPO on terminal and code-editing tasks.

On Qwen3-4B, GRPO from ActObs achieves higher pass@k at every evaluated sampling budget than action-only SFT on Terminal-Bench 2.0; on Qwen3-8B it trades some pass@1 for +3.4 pp pass@16, and cross-domain transfer to aider-polyglot improves +4.2 pp pass@1 at 4B. All claims are pass@k percentage-point deltas, not multiplicative factors.
